source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-16: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 16 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
For variant 16, treat resilience as a testable scheduler-and-recovery property, not an architectural claim. Assumptions: jobs declare GPU count/type, CPU, memory, storage, NIC/RDMA and topology needs, DP/TP parallelism, priority, checkpoint format/interval, and inference SLOs; inventory, placement, preemption, fencing, and failure events are observable; the platform’s actual capacities and semantics must be measured rather than assumed.

Hypothesis: topology-aware gang admission with fragmentation-aware packing, checkpoint-aware preemption, and bounded node-drain recovery will reduce wasted GPU-hours and training recovery time without worsening inference latency or availability, relative to the current first-fit policy. Keep workload mix, cluster inventory, model, checkpoint policy, and replica-routing policy fixed in matched baseline/canary windows. Inject one authorized, isolated node failure after a readiness check. Measure queue and admission time (s), GPU/NIC utilization (%), fragmentation (free GPU-hours unavailable to requested shapes), checkpoint interval and size (s/GB), recovery time (s), lost/replayed tokens or steps, failed work (GPU-hours), inference p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), error rate (%), throughput (tokens/s), SLO violations, and resource accounting by tenant/job. Report sample counts, confidence intervals, topology, units, and censoring rules.

Design the control plane around atomic gang reservations and GPU/NIC/NUMA/NVLink-aware placement; avoid treating aggregate free capacity as interchangeable. Use priority and preemption budgets with admission fairness, checkpoint integrity/version checks, and bounded checkpoint upload. Drain a node by fencing new work, quiescing or checkpointing jobs, verifying durable checkpoints, then restarting elastically only with a consistent membership/rendezvous state. Route inference only to healthy replicas with capacity-aware admission and fail closed rather than duplicate unsafe work. Reconcile scheduler allocations with device telemetry and charge actual reserved versus used resources.

The canary must be reversible: start with read-only inventory and placement tracing, then a small tenant-scoped rollout with rate and blast-radius limits. Roll back to the prior scheduler and stop fault injection if p95/p99 inference latency, error rate, checkpoint corruption, duplicate execution, recovery time, or fairness exceeds predeclared thresholds, or if fencing/audit evidence is incomplete. Do not claim causality until matched trials rule out workload mix, thermal/throttling, network congestion, storage, model, and concurrent maintenance confounders. Evidence should include versioned configurations, placement decisions, synchronized scheduler/device/storage/network traces, checkpoint hashes and restore logs, failure-injection records, and redacted audit/rollback logs.
risks: platform-specific topology, scheduler semantics, failure detection, and SLO baselines are unknown
preemption, restart, or routing can cause data loss, duplicate work, or unsafe service degradation if fencing and checkpoint coordination fail
fault injection can affect unrelated tenants without strict isolation
evidence_required: versioned scheduler, agent, checkpoint, and routing configuration
GPU/NIC/NUMA/topology inventory plus placement and reservation decisions
matched baseline/canary metrics with units, sample counts, confidence intervals, and confounder logs
checkpoint integrity hashes, fencing evidence, and failure-injection recovery traces
redacted audit trail and rollback record
